pairs.question: Dic quo iter inceptas; quis est quem arcessis?
pairs.derivation: Diniarchus asks Astaphium where she is going and whom she is fetching; she answers, naming the midwife Archilis. Stripped the dangling every-5-lines number 130 at the end of line 170 and the corruption marker ~ before 'obstetricem' at the start of line 171; the answer words themselves are clean. Answer ends at the first full stop, before Diniarchus's following retort 'Mala tu femina es...'.

pairs.question: Estne intus nunc Phronesium?
pairs.derivation: Diniarchus asks whether Phronesium is inside; Astaphium answers that whatever the case for others, for him she is inside. Both lie on a single source line; no scaffolding to strip. Answer is the whole reply (one sentence).

pairs.question: Valetne?
pairs.answer: Immo edepol melius iam fore spero, te ubi videbit.
pairs.derivation: Diniarchus asks whether Phronesium is well; Astaphium answers she will be better once she sees him. Whole reply is one sentence; nothing to cut, no scaffolding on this line.

pairs.question: Vbi cenabis?
pairs.derivation: Phronesium asks Diniarchus where he will dine; he answers 'wherever you order'. Stripped the dangling every-5-lines number 360 at the end of the source line. Answer is the complete reply.

pairs.question: Dic, amabo te, ubi est Diniarchus?
pairs.derivation: Phronesium asks Cyamus where Diniarchus is; he answers 'at home'. Single clean source line, no scaffolding. Answer is the one-word reply.

pairs.question: Quid isti debes?
pairs.derivation: Stratophanes asks Phronesium what she owes 'that fellow' (Strabax); she answers 'Tria' (three things). Self-contained one-word interrogative and reply on a single source line. Stopped before the follow-up 'Quae tria nam?' / 'Vnguenta, noctem, savium' so the question keeps its own complete answer; did not splice the two speakers' later lines into one field.
